Hi Monica,

Thanks for the call today. As part of Meridian Health's security intake for our pilot, the security team needs a short, bundled evidence packet confirming the following:

- Which Redwood-hosted model endpoints and inference capacity will be provisioned in the EU (preferred region: eu-west-1) vs. any US-hosted fallback.
- A CAIQ snapshot or SOC2 scope note covering inference and data-at-rest controls for the EU-hosted environment.
- A simple private-link / VPC peering diagram showing ingress/egress paths (we require evidence that traffic stays within EU egress boundaries).
- Confirmation of KMS key locality and whether customer-managed keys can be scoped to EU regions.
- An attestation letter we can include in our compliance artifacts, signed by an authorized Redwood representative.

Can you provide the evidence pack (PDF + network diagram + short attestation) by end of week? Also include any known limitations (e.g., batch processing fallback to non-EU nodes under extreme load).

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Ellison
Head of Infrastructure Security | Meridian Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2026-10-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-Boundary Confirmation & Private Link Audit Pack for Meridian Health

Monica / Irene —

Draft of the technical statements to include in the pack (feel free to copy/paste):

- Region hosting: Redwood will serve Meridian Health inference traffic from EU-primary capacity in eu-west-1 (AWS) for pinned deployments. For Hosted API usage, we route by customer region preference; our EU-hosted pool is configured to maintain all inference compute and KV cache within eu-west-1.

- Fallback behavior: In the event of capacity exhaustion in EU pools we support an automated fallback to a compatible model variant in us-east-1 only if the customer has opted into cross-region fallback in their deployment policy. We will state that Meridian's account is configured with cross-region-fallback = OFF by default for pilot.

- KV cache and tokenization: Persistent KV caches for pinned deployments remain in-region; ephemeral caches used in the hosted fleet are subject to routing policy and will not cross borders when cross-region-fallback is OFF.

- KMS: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed and customer-managed KMS keys. For customer-managed keys, CMKs must be provisioned in the same region as the host capacity (eu-west-1). We will include a CSV mapping of KMS key IDs and the region binding.

- Network topology: PrivateLink (AWS Interface VPC Endpoint) will terminate into our EU-hosted private NLB fronting the inference fleet. Traffic egress paths are restricted via route tables and egress policies to avoid US egress. Diagram attached.

I attached: redwood_CA_2026_CAIQ_snapshot.pdf (filtered), privatelink_connection_diagram.png, kms-region-mapping.csv.

If these statements look good I can sign-off on the technical attestation and Monica can handle the compliance language and signature.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie —

Attached is the Meridian evidence bundle we discussed. Overview: 

- redwood_CA_2026_CAIQ_snapshot.pdf — CAIQ excerpt focused on runtime/inference controls, encryption, and key management.
- privatelink_connection_diagram.png — VPC endpoint diagram showing private NLB termination in eu-west-1 and flow controls.
- kms-region-mapping.csv — Mapping of KMS key aliases to region bindings.
- redwood_data_locality_attestation.pdf — One-page attestation on Redwood letterhead.

Retention statement (one-liner to include in attestation): "For Meridian Health pilot accounts configured with EU-only hosting, inference request and ephemeral logs are stored and retained in eu-west-1. Default retention for ephemeral request logs is 30 days unless otherwise contractually specified."

DocuSign: We have initiated an envelope for the attestation. Link: https://app.docusign.com/documents/EMB-992183 (expected signature by Monday 2026-10-06).

Notes / limitations:
- Cross-region fallback is OFF for Meridian by default; if Meridian requests emergency cross-region failover under incident response, we will put a change request and notify security stakeholders.
- Long-running batch jobs that exceed EU capacity caps will be queued rather than fail-sent to other regions (this is documented in the attached CAIQ excerpt).

Next steps: Please confirm receipt and whether Meridian needs the full CAIQ (we can provide a full export under NDA). If DocuSign is acceptable, we'll share the signed PDF when complete.
